item.title: Pitino says 'selfish basketball' led to Xavier's 2nd-half struggles
item.description: Since an exhibition loss doesn't count against a team's record, what's the biggest risk in a preseason defeat? "I think we get a little carried away with exhibition games for the fear of people roasting us on Twitter," Xavier head coach Richard Pitino said after his Musketeers pulled out a 76-70 win over Kent State at Cintas Center Oct. 23. "That's what social media does. It puts everybody on edge because we don't wanna get crapped on all the time by everybody." Xavier avoided any social media overreactions by holding off Kent State Friday night in a tale of two halves. Xavier led, 37-28, at the intermission in a first-half performance that − despite a slow night offensively − looked like how a Big East team should handle a mid-major opponent. More: Xavier wraps up exhibition play at 3-0. Why it matters. The second half was a different story as Kent State took the lead on two occasions before a 10-4 Xavier run provided enough cushion for the Musketeers to complete a 3-0 month of exhibition play. What was the difference? "There was a moment in the second half with a little bit of selfish basketball, a little bit of effort lapses... I thought it was great for our guys to see," Pitino said. "There was a little moment in the second half where we were playing the wrong way. We corrected it, learned from it and pulled away." There's not one category on the box score one could point at to show Xavier's selfishness. The Musketeers did score 22 points in the paint in the first half but relied heavily on the 3-point shot (32 attempts). Xavier got four 3-pointers each from Jovan Milicevic and Ruben Dominguez, including some timely triples down the stretch. Xavier's starters combined for 61 points and 29 rebounds. Point guard Tru Washington and center Mike Nwoko were also in double figures while Filip Borovicanin flirted with a triple-double (8 points, 10 assists, 9 rebounds). On the glass, Xavier was outrebounded, 42-37, and gave up 12 second-chance opportunities. Kent State had a pair of 9-0 spurts in the first 12 minutes of the second half. The first tied the game at 37-37 immediately out of the locker room, the second gave the Golden Flashes their largest lead of the night (56-52) with 8:01 remaining. "They're exhibition games. I thought there were a lot of positives," Pitino said. "I thought today was really, really good. It revealed how, when we don't play the right way, how bad we make ourselves look." item.title: You had to be there to see it; even that was no guarantee
item.description: Many people will always remember the game at Woodmore in Week 10. That doesn't mean they were able to see it. A fog settled over the field and didn't dissipate as the Wildcats topped visiting Gibsonburg 45-14 to cap an unbeaten regular season with an outright championship in the Sandusky Bay Conference. Woodmore last won a conference crown in 1997 and was also 10-0 in 1995. The Wildcats won nine combined games in the 10 years before coach Scott Stecher's arrival three years ago. "It's like a blanket over us," Stecher said. "Like our own snow globe. This will be a happy moment (to remember) for the rest of their lives for them to relive." High school football It all comes down to this in SBC | Gibsonburg at Woodmore in Week 10 Lucas Caldwell raced 79 yards for a touchdown and 20-8 lead late in the third quarter. He ran in from 44 yards in the second quarter. "It's crazy; it's been so long," Caldwell said. "The program was at the bottom of the barrel -- it feels so special. It's most special because I did it with the guys I love the most. This is family. It's so special to do it with these guys. Wesley Kayser caught two touchdown passes and intercepted two throws on defense, including one he returned for a Woodmore score. Luke Karshner returned a fumble 37 yards for a touchdown and Ish Nagy scored from 50 yards out. Venerable Woodmore announcer Dave Robenstine exclaimed, 'Touchdown by 'somebody.' Earlier, an incomplete pass was thrown to 'somebody' in the fog. Caldwell and quarterback Calvin Lipstraw were also active on defense, with at least two tackles for a loss each. "I would already remember this for the rest of my life," Caldwell said. "Now, the way the fog showed up — every time I see fog, I'm going to think of this game." You had to be there to see it. If you were lucky. mhorn@gannett.com 419-307-4892 X: MatthewHornNH This article originally appeared on Fremont News-Messenger: You had to be there to see it; even that was no guarantee

item.description: Jacob Misiorowski did not have to wait long to feel the energy of the World Series. The Milwaukee Brewers right-hander recorded his first strikeout on baseball’s biggest stage Friday night, and the reaction from the crowd at American Family Field said everything about what the moment meant to Brewers fans. A video of the strikeout shows Misiorowski and the Milwaukee crowd getting fired up as the young pitcher continued his first World Series start. With the Brewers playing in their first Fall Classic since 1982, every big pitch carries a little extra weight, and the fans were ready to celebrate. Also Read: Who Is Front Row Amy? The 24-year-old put together a remarkable regular season, finishing with a 1.80 ERA and a major league-leading 252 strikeouts. His overpowering fastball has become his calling card, and he brought that same velocity to the World Series opener against the Tampa Bay Rays. The Brewers are chasing the first World Series title in franchise history, and Misiorowski is taking the ball in Game 1 with the hopes of an entire fan base behind him. The crowd’s reaction to that first strikeout was a reminder of just how much this run means to the city. The Brewers have waited decades to get back to this stage, and every strikeout, big play and moment of momentum feels that much bigger. item.title: Spurs bring Supreme, Balenciaga and Chrome Hearts to Austin ahead of Rockets showdown
item.description: Victor Wembanyama wears a Supreme x Nike Paneled Hoodie and matching sweatpants from the Fall/Winter 2026 collection ahead of Friday's game against the Houston Rockets. (Courtesy of San Antonio Spurs) The San Antonio Spurs turned the Moody Center into a fashion runway Friday night, with Victor Wembanyama, Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper and Devin Vassell showing off designer streetwear ahead of their I-35 showdown against the Houston Rockets. From Supreme and Nike to Balenciaga and Chrome Hearts, the Spurs brought plenty of style to the state capital before taking the court against their Texas rivals. Wembanyama kept things sporty, arriving in a white Supreme x Nike Paneled Hoodie and matching Paneled Sweatpants from the brands' Fall/Winter 2026 collection. The coordinated tracksuit featured bold red panels along the sleeves and legs. The 7-foot-4 French superstar completed his look with white Nikes. Castle mixed athletic apparel with luxury fashion, pairing a black Jordan zip-up hoodie with Balenciaga Baggy Sweatpants in "Off White/Black." The oversized pants featured black tattoo-inspired graphics against an off-white background. He finished the outfit with black footwear, a travel bag and a chain under the hoodie. Harper went with an all-black Chrome Hearts ensemble, sporting the luxury brand's Polar Fleece Plus Cross Patch Quarter Zip with matching Chrome Hearts sweatpants. The Spurs guard completed his understated look with black sneakers and a backpack. Vassell also represented Chrome Hearts, arriving in a blue-and-white Striped Collar Polo Shirt paired with faded jeans featuring the brand's signature black cross designs. He added a splash of color with Brain Dead x Converse Chuck 70 High sneakers in "Mismatched Prints," which featured contrasting patterns. The pregame fashion display came as San Antonio prepared to face Houston at Austin's Moody Center, bringing the Texas rivalry to the state capital. And while the Spurs were focused on delivering a win against the Rockets, Wembanyama and his teammates made sure to make a statement before tipoff. item.title: Shakur Stevenson's manager on Zuffa Boxing exit: We want people who 'honor their word'
item.description: Shakur Stevenson's stunning departure from Zuffa Boxing without having a single fight has stolen all of the headlines in boxing over the past week. Neither Stevenson nor anyone connected to Zuffa offered details regarding the reasons for Stevenson's release after it was announced on Monday . James "J" Prince, Stevenson's longtime manager, finally addressed the media for the first time on Friday. Prince explained to FightHubTV : "We want to move forward with relationships and situations where people honor their word and keep their word. That's important to us." "We had a contract, so the purses and different things were pretty much agreed upon. It was just getting an opponent. I think a lot of time was spent on the wrong opponent, which was Devin Haney. "I think Devin wanted the fight, I think Bill [Haney] didn't want the fight. And I think they figured out a way to sabotage the fight. It's interesting how you hear all of the lies and opinions that people have on what happened, but the reality of it is exactly what I just said." Stevenson, the reigning WBO super lightweight champion and Uncrowned’s No. 4 pound-for-pound boxer , claimed on social media that negotiations to face Haney broke down at the 11th hour because Haney insisted he would only fight at the welterweight limit of 147 pounds, instead of an agreed-upon 145-pound catchweight. Shakur Stevenson signed with Dana White's Zuffa Boxing in July. Ed Mulholland via Getty Images Haney responded by refuting the claim and saying he did agree to 145 pounds, but Stevenson then attempted to put a rehydration clause on him as well, which he would not accept. Said Prince: "That's part of the lies that's being told — no [rehydration] clause. We agreed at 145 [pounds], and Shakur was training for the fight. I was told Devin was training for the fight. item.title: Junior Caminero hit a ball so far in batting practice he took out Fox desk
item.description: Credit: Fox Tampa Bay Rays slugger Junior Caminero can hit some dingers. His shooting gave the Knicks a steady source of offense as they tried to climb back from a 10-point deficit entering the fourth quarter. item.description: Jayson Tatum Answers Rough Celtics Opener With Clutch Performance Against Knicks originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jayson Tatum gave the Celtics the response they needed Friday night. After a rough season opener, he scored 36 points and came through late as Boston held off the defending champion New York Knicks, 107-103, at TD Garden. Tatum added nine rebounds and seven assists, filling the box score while taking charge when the game tightened. The performance was a sharp turnaround from Tuesday’s loss to Detroit, when he finished with 13 points on 6-of-23 shooting. Tatum Took Control After Halftime The Celtics needed time to find their rhythm. Tatum had 11 points at the break, and Boston led by only one after two quarters. He found more space in the third, scoring 16 points as the Celtics put together their best stretch of the night and carried an 83-73 lead into the fourth. JAYSON TATUM TOOK OVER IN THE 4TH TO BEAT THE KNICKS 😳 36 PTS and the W! https://t.co/z2SrlW47He — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) October 24, 2026 That advantage nearly disappeared. New York kept pressing, and Jalen Brunson brought the Knicks within one point with 1:41 left. With the Celtics facing another tense finish after their season-opening collapse, Tatum answered with a difficult fallaway jumper to push Boston back in front. The Knicks continued to threaten, but Tatum kept responding. He hit a long two, then knocked down a three-pointer over Karl-Anthony Towns. Those baskets helped Boston protect its lead, and the Celtics held on for the four-point win. MORE : Why Mitchell Robinson Left Knicks for Celtics: Revisiting Center's Free Agency Decision Boston Gets A Different Ending Boston’s opener against Detroit ended with the Celtics surrendering a 22-point lead. Friday’s game brought a different kind of pressure: the Celtics had built a lead again, but this time had to make plays late to keep the Knicks from taking the game away. Tatum supplied those plays. Paul George and Neemias Queta added 15 points apiece, giving Boston important support, but it was Tatum who stopped New York’s late push. One win doesn’t erase the questions raised by the opener. The Celtics still have plenty to clean up, and the Knicks made them work for every possession down the stretch. But Tatum’s response was an encouraging sign: when Boston needed its star to take over, he did. item.title: Kenneth Walker III will be out for revenge when Chiefs take on Seahawks, but it won’t be easy
item.description: Kenneth Walker III will be out for revenge when Chiefs take on Seahawks, but it won’t be easy appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . One of the biggest matchups in the NFL in Week 7 pits the Kansas City Chiefs against the Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs’ resurgence has been one of the most notable storylines in the NFL this season, and now they will take their unbeaten record into one of the toughest places to play in the league against the defending Super Bowl champions. Of course, these two teams will be linked and compared all season long because of star running back Kenneth Walker III . Walker spent the first four seasons of his career with the Seahawks after they drafted him in the second round out of Michigan State, ultimately winning Super Bowl MVP last season after capping a monster playoff run with an excellent showing in the big game. This offseason, however, Walker departed Seattle for the Chiefs on a three-year, $43 million deal. The Chiefs badly needed to revamp their running game, and Walker has done just that . His insertion into Andy Reid’s offense has done wonders for Kansas City and is a big reason the Chiefs are 5-0. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) On the other side, the Seahawks have struggled mightily at running back without Walker this season. Zach Charbonnet is working his way back from a torn ACL, and first-round pick Jadarian Price is out with a chest injury. That has left the Seattle running back room barren, though it appears that Charbonnet will be back for Sunday’s game. There’s no question that Walker will be out for revenge on Sunday night against his old team. But it won’t be easy against what has once again been arguably the best defense in the NFL. Let’s get into the battle between two of the league’s best units set to take stage in prime time on Sunday night. Kenneth Walker has completely changed the Chiefs’ running game William Purnell-Imagn Images For the last few seasons, even when they were winning Super Bowls, the Chiefs have not had an explosive running game. Isiah Pacheco and Kareem Hunt have handled most of the carries for Andy Reid and company over the last few years, which just isn’t a way to threaten defenses on the ground. Walker has changed all of that. The reigning Super Bowl MVP has given the Chiefs that explosive element and currently leads the NFL with 665 yards and six touchdowns through five games. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . One of the biggest matchups in the NFL in Week 7 pits the Kansas City Chiefs against the Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs’ resurgence has been one of the most notable storylines in the NFL this season, and now they will take their unbeaten record into one of the toughest places to play in the league against the defending Super Bowl champions. Of course, these two teams will be linked and compared all season long because of star running back Kenneth Walker III . Walker spent the first four seasons of his career with the Seahawks after they drafted him in the second round out of Michigan State, ultimately winning Super Bowl MVP last season after capping a monster playoff run with an excellent showing in the big game. This offseason, however, Walker departed Seattle for the Chiefs on a three-year, $43 million deal. The Chiefs badly needed to revamp their running game, and Walker has done just that . His insertion into Andy Reid’s offense has done wonders for Kansas City and is a big reason the Chiefs are 5-0. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) On the other side, the Seahawks have struggled mightily at running back without Walker this season. Zach Charbonnet is working his way back from a torn ACL, and first-round pick Jadarian Price is out with a chest injury. That has left the Seattle running back room barren, though it appears that Charbonnet will be back for Sunday’s game. There’s no question that Walker will be out for revenge on Sunday night against his old team. But it won’t be easy against what has once again been arguably the best defense in the NFL. Let’s get into the battle between two of the league’s best units set to take stage in prime time on Sunday night. Kenneth Walker has completely changed the Chiefs’ running game William Purnell-Imagn Images For the last few seasons, even when they were winning Super Bowls, the Chiefs have not had an explosive running game. Isiah Pacheco and Kareem Hunt have handled most of the carries for Andy Reid and company over the last few years, which just isn’t a way to threaten defenses on the ground. Walker has changed all of that. The reigning Super Bowl MVP has given the Chiefs that explosive element and currently leads the NFL with 665 yards and six touchdowns through five games. He also has 95 yards and two scores through the air, so he is a big part of this offense no matter the situation. The numbers, especially when you contrast them with last year, make the difference especially glaring. Walker not only leads the league in rushing yards, but he also is No. 1 among running backs in EPA per rush (+0.13). He has 19 carries of 10 or more yards, the second-best mark in the NFL behind only James Cook. He also ranks second in yards after contact with 438, trailing only Bijan Robinson, and he has 277 rushing yards over expected, more than 100 more than Robinson in second place per Next Gen Stats. Now compare that to the Chiefs’ numbers last season. Kansas City had the seventh-best EPA per rush in the NFL in 2025 (+0.01). That’s a solid number, but it’s mostly a product of a solid run-blocking offensive line that is mostly intact this season. When you look at the numbers that speak more to how the individual runners are creating yards, it’s clear that the Chiefs needed an upgrade. The Chiefs ranked 27th in rush yards over expected last season and 31st in yards after contact per attempt, per Next Gen Stats. Their 44 rushes of 1o or more yards finished tied for 23rd, and Patrick Mahomes had 18 of those on scrambles. Mahomes is always going to do his thing, and Travis Kelce looks much better this season than he did in 2025. Even with Tyquan Thornton out for most of the season, the passing game is going to have its floor lifted by Mahomes. Now, the running game has both a high floor and a high ceiling, making this a very difficult offense to stop. If anyone can slow Walker down, it’s the Seahawks Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Walker has been almost unstoppable this season, but now he will go up against arguably the best defense in the NFL. Mike Macdonald led a historic unit a season ago that lifted this Seattle team to a Super Bowl, and while they have gone through some growing pains so far this season, this is still an elite unit. While they don’t quite have the world-beating numbers from a year ago at this point, the Seattle defense still tanks fourth in yards per rush allowed (3.5) and third in stuff rate (20.7%). Their -0.18 EPA per rush allowed also is the third-best mark in the NFL. A lot of that has to do with their defensive front, which is still one of the best in the NFL even as Leonard Williams works through an ankle injury. Seattle is allowing less than one yard before contact per rush from its opponents, one of the best marks in the league. Seattle has also been a very good tackling team, missing just 41 tackles in six games this season, per PFF. Walker has forced 41 missed tackles this season, by far the most in the NFL, so the battle between the two sides will be very intriguing to watch. Walker in the passing game could be a big key to the Chiefs moving the ball in this game. Macdonald defenses have struggled at times against running back screens dating back to his time against the Ravens, and that has been the case once again this season. Seattle has allowed the sixth-most backfield targets this season and the seventh-highest EPA per play on those plays per Next Gen Stats. Andy Reid has long been known as one of the best screen designers in football, and he has used that to weaponize Walker in the passing game. Look for him to get to that section of the call sheet early and often on Sunday night as the Chiefs look to get to 6-0. item.title: How a record night by receiver helped Metamora crush opponent in IHSA Class 4A playoffs
item.description: METAMORA — Survive and advance. Metamora opened its 2026 Illinois high school football playoff run with a 56-7 win over Alton Marquette on Friday, Oct. 23. This marks the fifth consecutive season Metamora has won at least one playoff game. The 12-seed Redbirds (7-3) now advance to next weekend's IHSA first round, heading to fifth-seeded Breese Central (8-1). This opening-round matchup also had a little bit of history for Metamora and Marquette (4-6). Metamora beat Alton Marquette in the 1975 Class 3A first round, becoming the Redbirds' first-ever playoff opponent on its way to the program's first state championship. More history was produced by Metamora receiver Briggs Bucy, whose second TD catch of the game set a school record for single-season touchdown catches at 12. He added a third TD catch to extend that record to 13. This story will be updated. item.title: Tatum delivers as Celtics down winless Knicks
item.description: Jayson Tatum celebrates after scoring in the fourth quarter of Boston's victory over the New York Knicks at TD Garden (Maddie Meyer) Jayson Tatum scored 36 points as the Boston Celtics defeated the New York Knicks 107-103 to leave the NBA champions waiting for their first win of the season on Friday. Tatum, back at full fitness after missing most of last season with a ruptured Achilles, delivered a mesmerizing performance at the TD Garden to give Boston their first win of the campaign after an opening-day loss to Detroit. The six-time NBA All-Star shot 14-of-26 from the field, including three three-pointers, with nine rebounds, seven assists and three steals. Nine of Tatum's points came in the fourth quarter as the Knicks, who had trailed by as many as 12 points early in the final frame, closed to within one point. Tatum's superb all-round display earned words of admiration from Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla. "That was a really well-balanced game from JT on both ends, and you were able to kind of see his greatness," Mazzulla said after the home opener. Tatum received scoring support from new signing Paul George and Neemius Queta, who both finished with 15 points apiece. The Knicks were led by 22 points from Karl-Anthony Towns, with OG Anunoby and Miles McBride scoring 20 each. Knicks talisman Jalen Brunson chipped in with 19. In other games Friday, the Minnesota Timberwolves stayed unbeaten with a 115-93 defeat of the Orlando Magic on the road. Minnesota's new-look offense, with Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball working in tandem, produced a balanced scoring display that saw seven players finish in double figures. Edwards and Jaden McDaniels each netted 15 points to top the scoring. Orlando fell to 0-2 with the loss. Elsewhere, the Atlanta Hawks moved to 2-0 with a 128-81 drubbing of the Charlotte Hornets, with Jalen Johnson and Aaron Wiggins scoring 19 points each. The Toronto Raptors are also unbeaten thanks to a 112-102 defeat of the Washington Wizards on the road. Scottie Barnes scored 28 points for Toronto with RJ Barrett adding 23 and Kawhi Leonard 16. Kyrie Irving's 24-point haul helped the Dallas Mavericks to a 121-105 defeat of the Indiana Pacers while the Milwaukee Bucks were left waiting for their first win of the campaign after falling 132-125 to the Chicago Bulls at home. rcw/js

item.title: Robin Yount throws emotional 1st pitch before World Series clash vs. Rays
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images Robin Yount throws emotional 1st pitch before World Series clash vs. Rays appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 2026 World Series began Friday in Milwaukee at American Family Field. It marked the first time the Brewers played in the Fall Classic since 1982. Before the first official pitch against the Tampa Bay Rays, Brewers legend Robin Yount was slated to throw out the ceremonial first pitch before a packed house, per Bob Nightengale of USA Today. It was an emotional moment for more than one reason. Former MLB Commissioner and Brewers owner Bud Selig handed Yount the ball. Additionally, Young wore a Bob Uecker jacket, in honor of the beloved broadcaster who passed away in 2025. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Emotional first pitch ceremony with Bud Selig handing baseball to Hall of Famer Robin Yount, who dons a Bob Uecker sports jacket, takes it off, bows to the Uecker seat, and wears a Uecker jersey pic.twitter.com/JZcXMjvjTQ — Bob Nightengale (@BNightengale) October 24, 2026 Yount is one of the most legendary players in franchise history. He was part of the 1982 team that reached the World Series against the St. Louis Cardinals. That year, he won his first MVP as a shortstop. In the World Series, the Brewers lost to the Cardinals in seven games. In 1989, Yount won his 2nd MVP after moving to center field. Altogether, Yount played in MLB from 1974 to 1993. He finished his career with 3,142 hits, a .285 lifetime batting average, 251 home runs, 1406 RBIs, and 1,632 runs scored. He was a 3-time All-Star (1980, 1982, 1983), a 1982 Gold Glove winner, and a 3-time Silver Slugger Award winner (1980, 1982, 1989). In 1999, Yount was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame in Cooperstown. Meanwhile, the Brewers are looking to win their first World Series in franchise history. The same is true of the Tampa Bay Rays. The Brewers finished the season at 103-59, won the National League Central Division title, and swept the defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS. The roughly 40-minute show drew hundreds of fans to watch Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy and other colorful personalities from the media company. It featured game predictions, contests, pizza talk and the playful back-and-forth with fans that has become a hallmark of the show. For fans, the event brought a burst of attention to a program more accustomed to playing second fiddle to its basketball brethren. "UConn has a big college basketball program, but besides that, football is definitely an afterthought," said John Palot, a UConn senior from Newington. "So I think this is huge for UConn football. I love it." Mike Scarlett, a 40-year-old HVAC worker from Plainville, said he has been a UConn season-ticket holder since 2001 and described himself as a "stoolie," or dedicated Barstool follower. "Every game matters, but I think with Barstool being here, it's going to boost this program," he said. "It brings a lot of attention to UConn sports." item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — Illini fans came to State Farm Center Friday night expecting an encouraging exhibition win for Illinois’ first home game of the season. The outcome had a lot more to it than that. With David Mirkovic seen back in a boot and scooter during pregame warmups, Illinois fans didn’t think Friday night could get much worse—but it did. Facing off against Baylor’s fire-powered offense, shooting 61% from 3-point range in the first half and tallying *63* first-half points, neither Illinois’ offense nor defense was able to keep up at the start. However, Illinois began mounting a comeback out of the tunnel in the second half. They picked it up big time, riding a wave of momentum from an Andrej Stojakovic corner-three and slam dunk out of the tunnel. They improved on the boards, they took care of the ball and they finally found a way to slow down the Bears offense, holding them to just 32 second-half points. But as Illinois inched closer, the injuries piled up. Zvonimir Ivisic and Stojakovic both were shaken up after hard falls, seemingly head injuries. They both went to the locker room and did not return. Illinois nearly pulled off a magical second-half comeback after trailing by 19 at halftime, but fans ultimately walked home with frowns on their faces after Illinois fell to Baylor 95-91 and lost multiple key players to injury on the same night. With David Mirkovic seen back in a boot and scooter during pregame warmups, Illinois fans didn’t think Friday night could get much worse—but it did. Facing off against Baylor’s fire-powered offense, shooting 61% from 3-point range in the first half and tallying *63* first-half points, neither Illinois’ offense nor defense was able to keep up at the start. However, Illinois began mounting a comeback out of the tunnel in the second half. They picked it up big time, riding a wave of momentum from an Andrej Stojakovic corner-three and slam dunk out of the tunnel. They improved on the boards, they took care of the ball and they finally found a way to slow down the Bears offense, holding them to just 32 second-half points. But as Illinois inched closer, the injuries piled up. Zvonimir Ivisic and Stojakovic both were shaken up after hard falls, seemingly head injuries. They both went to the locker room and did not return. Tomislav Ivisic limped off the court midway through the second half, but was able to return to the bench. #illini Andrej Stojakovic going to locker room after a hard fall pic.twitter.com/iq3sYEmFCr — Carson Gourdie (@GourdieReport) October 24, 2026 Despite these three injuries, Illinois stayed determined. Lincoln Williams, Quentin Coleman, Ethan Brown, Jake Davis and Jason Jakstys kept the Illini chugging along, cutting the deficit to just four points with a few minutes left, but the comeback ultimately fell just short. Illinois felt preseason All-American selection David Mirkovic’s absence, struggling on the boards and in the paint. Head coach Brad Underwood consistently emphasizes the importance of offensive rebounding and second-chance buckets, and Illinois thrived at getting back a big chunk of its misses last season. But Friday night, Baylor beat Illinois with its own poison, winning the rebound battle and second-chance points battle. Freshman guard Quentin Coleman did his best to keep the Illini afloat, leading the scoring with 20 points, seven rebounds and six assists. Before his hard fall, Andrej Stojakovic tallied 15 points and knocked down six free throws, continuing to flash his ability to drive to the rim and draw fouls. Freshman Ethan Brown put up another solid statline and impressed yet again with seven points, two rebounds and two assists. After slow starts in the first half, Stefan Vaaks and Jake Davis picked up the scoring in the second in hopes of finishing off the comeback, combining for 23 second-half points. On offense, Illinois’ early turnovers and missed shots cost them. On defense, lack of rebounds and aggression in the paint played a factor, but the main cause of the first half deficit was simply Baylor catching fire from range. Stat Stuffers Kayden Mingo: 24 points, four rebounds and four assists Isaac Williams: 28 points, 11-20 FG, 3-5 3FG Stefan Vaaks: 18 points, five assists, 4-8 3FG Jake Davis: 10 points, three rebounds, four assists, 3-4 3FG Up Next Illinois will host UIC at State Farm Center Oct. 28 for its last exhibition matchup before the season kicks off.

item.title: NASCAR Truck Series championship down to two with two to go
item.description: Motorsport photo The Truck Series championship is as it always was following the triultimate race of the season at Talladega Superspeedway. Neither Kaden Honeycutt nor Layne Riggs won but raced around each other all race, scoring nearly identical stage points, and the deficit is 43 with just Martinsville and Homestead-Miami left. Technically, Ty Majeski , Chandler Smith and Christian Eckes are mathematically eligible but these scenarios require the two most dominant teams of the 2026 season to score the bare minimum points and one of those three to sweep stages and win races the next two weeks. Everyone knows the score. It’s the Tricon 11 versus the Front Row 34. Riggs had a chance to win on Friday, and it even came with forcing Honeycutt to push him out to the lead, but it didn’t work out for either driver. The final restart scenario gave Honeycutt a great deal of anxiety, however. When asked, he covered his face, and said that's what he wanted to do coming to the green. What does he do? "Race for the win, man," Honeycutt said. "I wasn't going to impede my own race by not pushing him. And I think my move in 1 and 2, it solely wasn't because I was trying to shuffle him out of line. It was he opened up the middle by a lot. So I thought if he moved up and I moved with him, I would've got shuffled out from the middle and I'd have lost my spots. "So yeah, just made a good move there to get back to the middle and have a shot to win. I just made it too early and too egregious, too much short track eagerness inside my body and just wanted to take it to him when I got it and just needed to be patient. I need to get better on this type of racing. But we'll take it. We'll move on to Martinsville now." Ultimately, Honeycutt finished fifth and Riggs eighth, so now Riggs more than likely needs to win these next two races at a minimum to claim the championship. “Yeah, that's where we're at,” Riggs said. “Unless the 11 has a really bad day. … “If he would've won today, we would've pretty much been done. I feel like I put in my head, if we're 45 or worse back, we probably didn't have a shot. “We're at 43 right now, so obviously it's not too much better. We're going to have to bring some bullets to the next two races. And I got full faith that Dylan (Capello), my crew chief and everybody can put their heads together and build a really, really fast truck these next two races.” Honeycutt isn’t counting points. “I've seen people make up 90 in two races, so nothing is safe for sure,” Honeycutt said. And Riggs is both a short tracker that has spent a decade racing at Martinsville and is confident for Homestead. “Martinsville's great,” Riggs said. “We were on the pole last year, had a transmission issue and I still felt like we had a winning truck. So, I'm excited about that (and) what we can do. “And then Homestead, we ran really well there last year in the early season as well. So me and Kyle Larson were battling and Corey (Heim) was up front, had really good trucks.

item.title: Brandon Miller Struggles in Hornets' Blowout Loss to Hawks
item.description: The Charlotte Hornets were blown out by the Atlanta Hawks on Friday night, losing 128-81. It was a disappointing game after the Hornets had secured a 110-103 win over the Brooklyn Nets in their season opener. Star forward Brandon Miller was a major contributor to their struggles, as he had six points, two rebounds, two steals, a block, and two turnovers, shooting 2-for-14 from the field and 1-for-11 from three. Miller inked a five-year, $209 million extension in the offseason with the Hornets, but hasn't played well to start the 2026-27 season. Through two games, he is averaging 12 points, 2.5 rebounds, 0.5 assists, a steal, a block, and 2.5 turnovers per game while shooting 25.7 percent from the floor and 12.5 percent from deep. Charlotte will look to get more out of their star in the coming games, as he is a focal point for their future success. Miller should have some pressure eased off him once his co-star, Kon Knueppel, is back on the floor. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Knueppel is one of the team's best offensive players, as he had a strong 2025-26 season, finishing second in Rookie of the Year voting. He averaged 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 3.4 assists while shooting 47.5 percent from the floor and 42.5 percent from three-point range. Getting Knueppel and guard Coby White back in the lineup will help the offense find a flow and could spark Miller to get back into a rhythm. Miller wasn't the only one who struggled, as it was an all-around abysmal performance by the Hornets' offense. They shot 34 percent from the field and 22 percent from behind the arc while turning the ball over 25 times. Naz Reid was in double figures with 17 points, six rebounds, two assists, and a steal, shooting 7-for-16 from the floor and 3-for-8 from downtown, but he turned the ball over seven times. Grayson Allen and Tidjane Salaun were the other two players in double digits for Charlotte, with 11 points apiece. While the offense was bad, the defense wasn't great either for the Hornets. Atlanta shot 51 percent from the field and 40 percent from three, with seven Hawks players scoring double-digit points. There aren't many positives to take away from this game for Charlotte. Charles Lee will look to get his group back on track ahead of their matchup on Saturday against the Miami Heat.

item.title: Packers vs. Lions Preview: Rivals Face Crucial NFC North Test
item.description: Photo by: Mark J. Rebilas The Green Bay Packers are preparing for one of their biggest tests of the season as they travel to Ford Field to take on the Detroit Lions on Sunday afternoon. With both teams fighting for position in the NFC North, this Week 7 matchup could have major implications for the division race. Green Bay enters the game with a 4-2 record and plenty of momentum after winning three consecutive games. The Packers are coming off a 23-13 victory over the Dallas Cowboys, a performance that showcased their ability to make plays on both sides of the football. Detroit, meanwhile, enters at 3-2 after its bye week and will be looking to make a statement against one of its biggest divisional rivals. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. Jordan Love Leads Green Bay’s Offense Quarterback Jordan Love will be one of the biggest factors in Sunday’s game. Love has been playing well recently, throwing for 643 yards and three touchdowns over his last two games against Chicago and Dallas. The Packers’ passing attack has become a major strength, with Christian Watson and Matthew Golden providing explosive options downfield. Green Bay will need those receivers to create separation against Detroit’s secondary and help Love generate big plays. Tight end Tucker Kraft could also play an important role, particularly in the red zone. Love has demonstrated the ability to attack defenses at multiple levels, and the Packers will need another efficient performance from their quarterback to keep pace with Detroit. The biggest question for Green Bay is its rushing attack. The Packers have struggled to establish consistency on the ground, making the potential availability of running back Josh Jacobs an important storyline heading into Sunday. If Jacobs can return and provide a spark, Green Bay could have a more balanced offensive approach. Detroit Looks to Protect Home Field The Lions enter this matchup rested after their bye week, giving head coach Dan Campbell and his staff additional time to prepare for Green Bay. Quarterback Jared Goff will lead an offense featuring running back Jahmyr Gibbs and wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown. Detroit has the offensive firepower to challenge Green Bay’s defense, particularly if it can establish the run and create opportunities for explosive passes. The Packers’ defense will need to limit big plays and keep Gibbs from consistently breaking into the second level. Forcing Detroit into third and long situations could help Green Bay generate pressure and create opportunities for turnovers.

McConnell #9 of the Indiana Pacers in action during the game against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on March 17, 2026 in New York City. The Knicks won 136-110. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) Getty The Indiana Pacers are a lot healthier this season than they were last season, starting with superstar Tyrese Haliburton. But not all of their players have avoided injuries in the early going, and the Pacers were without two members of their backcourt in the season opener in T.J. McConnell and Aaron Nesmith. Indiana is playing its second game of the season on Friday night against the Dallas Mavericks, and the Pacers will be missing McConnell again. The good news is that Nesmith is back from a left hamstring strain. More bad news popper up, though, as Ben Sheppard is out. Rick Carlisle says that Aaron Nesmith is playing tonight. Ben Sheppard is going to be OUT for a little bit. Carlisle says no timetable for his return. Could be two weeks, could be longer. https://t.co/j35Q9voxOj — Alex Golden (@AlexGoldenNBA) October 23, 2026 Here’s what we know about McConnell specifically. Why Isn’t T.J. McConnell Playing Tonight? McConnell is sidelined for the second consecutive game due to injury. He has been listed by the Pacers with a right hamstring strain. It wasn’t immediately clear during the preseason why McConnell wasn’t playing, but he didn’t appear in a preseason game. When the Pacers officially listed McConnell on the injury report for Wednesday’s season opener, that’s when the full diagnosis of right hamstring strain was made available. The worst part of this is that hamstring problems forced McConnell to miss 26 games last season, and he’s now 34, so his body might be letting him down a bit. There’s no way to know whether it’s the same hamstring problem, but the recurrence or new appearance of more hamstring issues is not ideal for McConnell. He’s a fan favorite, to be sure, and the Pacers get a jolt every time McConnell comes off the bench. For now, though, he has to stay on the bench, because he isn’t healthy enough to get on the court. Pacers’ Replacements for T.J. McConnell The Pacers can certainly let Haliburton handle most of the point guard minutes since he’s healthy. When Haliburton isn’t in the game, Andrew Nembhard can help run the point. Sheppard could’ve too, but now he’s hurt. The Pacers also got 16 quality minutes in the opener out of guard Quenton Jackson, who has six points, four rebounds and three steals. As long as Haliburton stays healthy, the McConnell absence hurts the Pacers’ vibes but maybe doesn’t crush the rotation all that much at this point. item.title: Sammy Smith Wins Wild Talladega Truck Series Race in Dramatic Finish
item.description: Photo by: Mark J. Rebilas Sammy Smith delivered a memorable performance at Talladega Superspeedway on Friday, capturing his first career NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series victory after a thrilling finish in the Love’s RV Stop 225. Driving the No. 7 Chevrolet for Spire Motorsports, Smith made a decisive move on the final lap of overtime to secure the victory in one of the most dramatic finishes of the season. The win was especially significant because it came just hours after Smith announced he would compete full-time in the Truck Series with TRICON Garage in 2027. Smith appeared to be on the outside looking in during the closing moments, running behind the leaders as Ty Majeski and Kaden Honeycutt battled for the top position. However, a strong push from Tyler Ankrum helped Smith surge forward and make his move coming through the final turns. Smith powered past the leaders and held on at the finish line, beating Ankrum by just 0.091 seconds. Austin Green finished third, followed by Majeski and Honeycutt. The victory marked Smith’s first Truck Series win in just his 11th career start. He also led a race-high 21 laps, demonstrating the speed of the No. 7 Chevrolet throughout the afternoon. The race was far from smooth sailing, as Talladega once again delivered the kind of unpredictable action that makes superspeedway racing so entertaining. Multiple cautions and major multi-truck incidents created challenges throughout the event, with several drivers seeing their days end early. Among those caught in an early crash were NASCAR veteran Tony Stewart and motorsports personality Cleetus McFarland. Both drivers were eliminated from contention following the incident. Despite the chaos, Smith and his team remained in position to capitalize when the opportunity presented itself. His late charge through the field ultimately made the difference in a finish that featured multiple trucks fighting for the win. The victory also provides Smith with plenty of momentum heading into the next chapter of his NASCAR career. After spending recent seasons competing full-time in the NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series, he is preparing to move to TRICON Garage for a full-time Truck Series campaign next season. Smith will take over the No. 15 Toyota for TRICON in 2027, giving him an opportunity to build on his growing NASCAR résumé while competing for wins on a regular basis. Winning at Talladega before beginning that new chapter makes Friday’s result even more meaningful. Smith has already shown he can compete at the front of the Truck Series field, and his ability to execute under pressure could make him a driver to watch next season. For now, Smith can celebrate a breakthrough victory that capped off an eventful day and gave him his first Truck Series trophy. With a dramatic last-lap pass and a new full-time opportunity ahead, the Talladega win could be an important milestone in his racing career.

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
